summary: # Marvelous Designer Tips Sharing: Clothing Details Edition - Update P18 ## Introduction Hello everyone! Today, we are going to learn how to use the Selection Grid Tool to address the issue of clothes passing through the model. Since we are focusing on the Selection Grid Tool, let's first discuss some basic knowledge about it. ## Selection Grid Tool Overview ### Accessing the Tool To begin, select the mouse and choose the Grid Brush Tool. In the drop-down menu, you will find three Selection Grid Tools available for use: 1. **Selection Grid Brush**: - Use this tool by pressing the left mouse button on the board and dragging to highlight the selected area. - There are various additional functions accessible via the right mouse button in the selected area. ### Functions of the Selection Grid Brush - **Dividing Selected Parts**: The selected part of the grid can be divided into details, and the selected area can be converted into a fixed frame. - **Movement and Shaping**: You can move or shape the selected area. - **Soft Selection**: The darker the selected area, the stronger the application effect will be. ### Brush Settings - **Strength**: This determines the intensity of the effect during the painting process. A higher number indicates a stronger selection effect, while a lower number provides a softer effect. - **Size**: This refers to the area selected by the brush, with the focus being on the center of the brush. - **Focus**: A higher focus value results in a smaller reduction area, while a lower focus value increases the reduction part. > Note: The Selection Grid Brush function cannot move or rotate the grid. Its primary function is to select the grid, after which you can use the right mouse button for additional actions. ## Selection Grid Comparison Function ### Using the Function To use the Selection Grid Comparison function, follow these steps: 1. In the 3D window, hold down the left mouse button and drag the mouse to select the grid that needs modification. 2. The selected area will be highlighted in green and will also reflect in the 2D and 3D windows. ### Canceling Selections - Click on the 2D or 3D background to cancel the selection grid. - Click on a grid top to select only one grid top. - Click on a grid top on a line to select the entire line. - Double-click on the grid in the version to select the grid top of the entire version. ### Multiple Selections To select multiple grid tops at the same time: - Hold down the CTRL and SHIFT keys to stop selecting and then select all desired grid tops. - If you only press SHIFT while selecting, the currently selected grid will be canceled, and the unselected grid will be selected. - If you only press CTRL, the selected grid will be canceled. ### Moving and Rotating Selected Areas After selecting the grid, you can move or rotate the selected area by positioning the ball. The center of rotation will be determined by where you clicked when selecting the grid. ### Simulation Reset Once you have adjusted the grid position, turn on the simulation. The board will reset the simulation and return to the correct simulation position. ## Advanced Grid Adjustments ### Deep-Layer Fixing Pin If the selected grid area is converted into a fixing pin, then after opening the simulation, this area will not revert to its original position; it will remain fixed in 3D space. You can right-click on the fixing pin area to delete any extra fixing pins. ### Comparing Select Grid Functions The difference between the Select Grid and Select Grid Comparison tools lies in the method of selecting the grid. The Select Grid Comparison tool allows you to use a mouse to draw a locking area and then select the grid peak within that area. ## Addressing Hand Insertion Issues In the process of using the Select Grid tool to adjust grid peaks, keep in mind that you can only select the grids visible in the current view. If the grid is obstructed by other objects in the 3D space, such as a virtual model, you won't be able to select it simultaneously. ### Selecting Grids in 3D Space To mitigate this issue: 1. Select the grid in the 3D space first, referring to the position of the green height. 2. Then, in the 2D window, select the grid that needs modification within the frame and move it back to the 3D window, avoiding the problem of invisible grids. ### Fine-Tuning Adjustments Repeat the previous operation: 1. Select the grid in the 2D window. 2. Return to the 3D window and use the positioning ball to pull these grids out slightly, ensuring they do not intersect with the hand. You can make large adjustments first and then refine them in smaller increments. After turning on the simulation, wait for the panel to gradually simulate back to the original position. ## Adjusting Sleeves To adjust the sleeve on the other side: 1. Lift the sleeve up first to align the sleeve panel with the wrist position. 2. Once aligned, pause the simulation and select the grid as before, using the previous height reference. ### Ensuring Proper Alignment Once you have selected the grid in both the 3D and 2D spaces, pull the grid out slightly to prevent it from intersecting with the wrist. Press the control button to start the simulation and wait for it to stabilize. ## Coordinate System Adjustments If the positioning ball you are using differs from the coordinate system demonstrated in this video, it may be set to the default screen coordinate. To align it: 1. Right-click in the 3D background. 2. Select the positioning ball and choose the world coordinate to match the video, which is based on world coordinates. > Note: The default screen coordinate is based on the camera view, while world coordinates are based on the 3D view. ## Conclusion Thank you for joining me today! I hope you found these tips on using the Selection Grid Tool helpful. See you next time. Bye-bye!
